title: GIS-Integrated Digital Twin for 5G/6G Energy Efficient Base Station
summary: Amrita University proposes a network digital twin that combines geographic data with AI-supported radio adjustments to run 5G and 6G base stations on less energy; no measured result is reported.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The proposal connects Open Radio Access Network (OpenRAN) information with geographic data and AI-supported radio adjustments. Better responsiveness, coverage, and energy efficiency are intended outcomes. The source does not report a measured change in an operating network. The team names Amrita University, ESRI ArcGIS, the Indian Institute of Science and the Indian Open Source Mobile Congress as partners. Its future work lists the integration of ArcGIS into the 5G core and a digital twin proof of concept. No later report of either appears.
purpose: Adapt radio-network configurations to geographic and demand changes.

data.answer:
Amrita University combines GIS data and a network digital twin to explore more adaptive and energy-efficient base-station operation.

The proposed integration supplies no deployed control experiment, energy measurement, coverage tradeoff, or comparison with conventional radio tuning. OpenRAN and geographic data integration alone do not establish an AI benefit.

The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.
